labeller: labeller 2: claude-opus-5-5 through `claude -p` with every tool switched off (`--tools ""`), no MCP server (`--strict-mcp-config` with an empty config), no settings sources and no session persistence, run from an empty directory; given only labelling/2140/labeller-2-prompt.txt (seed 21402): policy-v1 and the 8 requirements added for #2140 (OS-26 to OS-33) in a seeded order. It saw no label, no rule summary, no code, no prompt of the product and no arm. It is not the agent that chose the requirements.

applies.reason: The initial user password must be at least 12 characters, which exceeds the 8-character minimum.
The initial account password is set at creation, but nothing says it is checked against a list of common passwords.
applies.businessFact: Is the initial user password checked against a list of at least the top 3000 common passwords during setup?

applies.reason: A forced change at first login stops the default password becoming long-term, but nothing says it is random or expires.
applies.businessFact: Are new users' default passwords unique and securely randomly generated, and do they expire after a short period?

applies.reason: The requirement asks for a mandatory TOTP step at first login, which gives multi-factor authentication.
The fix concerns the portal password change flow but does not say whether the current password is required.
applies.businessFact: Does the portal password change flow (with email used as username) require the patient's current password as well as the new one?

applies.reason: A copyable or emailed one-time login link carries the login secret in the URL.
The links are one-time, but nothing says whether they are securely random or expire after a short period.
applies.businessFact: Are third-party invitation tokens securely randomly generated, and do they expire after a short period even if never used?

applies.reason: Turning off the forced change lets the initial password created from the medical record become the patient's long-term password.
Credentials are created by staff, and with no forced change the staff member keeps knowing the patient's password.
The proposed one-time auto-login may put a login token in the URL.
applies.businessFact: Would the one-time auto-login token be carried in the URL or query string, or in the request body or headers?

applies.reason: Signing an encounter will rely on Google SSO, but nothing says the app checks the IdP's authentication time or method for this function.
applies.businessFact: When an encounter is signed through Google SSO, does the application require and verify a fresh authentication (for example the auth_time claim) from the IdP?

applies.reason: The password update is made independent of the username update, but nothing says it still requires the current password.
applies.businessFact: Will the separate password update on the portal credential settings page require the patient's current password as well as the new one?

applies.reason: Patients can change their username and password, but nothing says they are notified afterwards.
applies.businessFact: Is the patient notified, for example by email, after their portal username or password is changed?

applies.reason: Nothing says patients are offered the option to end other sessions after a password change.
applies.businessFact: After a portal password change, is the patient offered the option to terminate all other active sessions?

applies.reason: An administrator starts the portal credential reset, but the text does not say whether the administrator can see or choose the new password.
applies.businessFact: Does the administrator-initiated portal reset send the patient a reset process or link, rather than a password the administrator can see or set?

applies.reason: The reset sends system-generated portal credentials, but nothing says whether they are securely random, follow the password policy, or expire after first use.
applies.businessFact: Are the reset credentials emailed to the patient securely randomly generated, and do they expire after a short time or on first use?
